title: Count Submatrices That Sum to Target
statement: You are auditing a rectangular ledger stored as matrix, a list of rows where every row has the same number of integer entries (values may be negative, zero, or positive). Given matrix and an integer target, count how many non-empty axis-aligned submatrices have entries that add up to exactly target. A submatrix is any contiguous block chosen by picking a top row, a bottom row (at or below the top), a left column, and a right column (at or below the left); two submatrices are considered different if they occupy different row/column boundaries, even if their entries are identical. Return the count as a single integer. If matrix is empty or has no columns, return 0.
hints: Fixing a left and right column collapses each row into a single number (the sum of that row between those columns). What 1D problem does counting blocks that sum to target then become?

For each pair of column boundaries, walk down the rows keeping a running vertical sum and a hashmap of how many times each running-sum value has appeared, seeded with {0: 1}; a submatrix ending at the current row hits target whenever running - target was seen before.

Build row-wise prefix sums so any horizontal strip sum is O(1). Loop over every (c1, c2) column pair; for EACH pair create a FRESH prefix_counts = {0: 1}, reset running = 0, then for each row add strip = row_prefix[r][c2+1] - row_prefix[r][c1] to running, add prefix_counts[running - target] to the answer, and increment prefix_counts[running]. Summing over all column pairs gives the total.
